subject: Notes from your call with Ctm IT SUPPORT 0330 500 1215 on 24/09/2026 09:55
body_content:
Notes

Dear Giles Hugo,

Here’s the notes from your call with Ctm IT SUPPORT 0330 500 1215 on 24 September 2026 at 09:55:

This call involved Giles Hugo reporting a suspected malware incident following a phishing email, discussing ongoing scans, device status, and plans for device quarantine and potential re-imaging with support from CTM IT cybersecurity team. The call concluded with arrangements to drop off the affected device for a full wipe and investigation.

Recap

  • Giles Hugo's device was involved in opening a phishing email, which may have resulted in malware infection; the device is currently offline and disconnected from the network.
  • An offline full scan was initiated on Giles Hugo's laptop, which is a company device not linked to the organization's management system, and contains data backed up on Dropbox and OneDrive.
  • The device encountered BitLocker encryption prompting for a recovery key, which Giles Hugo does not possess, and he chose to skip the drive encryption prompt to continue scanning.
  • Support staff from CTM IT's cybersecurity team, including Zack, was consulted to assess the malware threat, confirm if the device is compromised, and discuss options for device remediation.
  • It was determined that the device should be completely wiped and possibly returned to the support team for re-imaging, as malware could be embedded deeply and may not be removable remotely.
  • Giles Hugo plans to deliver the device to CTM IT support in Cambridge for a full wipe, pending confirmation of costs and procedures, and will await further instructions.
  • Sign-in logs from Azure indicate recent activity from Giles Hugo's mobile device, but no suspicious or unauthorized access was detected from the organization's email system.
  • The support team advised that, due to the device not being managed or linked to the organization's system, remote isolation or quarantine is limited, and physical return for re-imaging is preferred.

Tasks

  • Giles Hugo will send the suspicious email to CTM IT support for analysis.
  • CTM IT support (Zack) will confirm the cost and process for device re-imaging and inform Giles Hugo.
  • Giles Hugo will drive the device to CTM IT support in Cambridge once instructed.
  • CTM IT support will verify if any malicious activity has been detected via Azure or email logs and will inform Giles Hugo accordingly.
  • Giles Hugo will await further instructions from CTM IT support regarding the device's remediation and re-imaging process.
